h1: Renovation at Scale for Servicers, REITs, Funds, Banks and GSEs
lede: Institutional owners do not need another local contractor. They need one accountable renovation partner that can take on volume across many markets, meet vendor compliance requirements, produce bids that can be approved remotely and deliver documentation that stands up to audit. Genstone Construction works with mortgage servicers, REITs, investment funds, banks and other lenders, and is a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises, with a footprint across 35 states.

sections.body:
Renovating one house well is a construction problem. Renovating hundreds of houses across many markets, under approval limits and reporting rules, is an operations problem. Most of what goes wrong at institutional scale is not workmanship. It is inconsistent bids, missing documentation, slow approvals, contractors whose insurance lapsed, invoices that do not match what was approved, and asset managers who cannot get a straight answer about status without making several phone calls.

Genstone Construction was built to solve that operations problem. Our clients include mortgage servicers, Real Estate Investment Trusts, investment funds, banks managing REO portfolios and other mortgage lenders. We are a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises. The Genstone Companies have been named to the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies two years in a row, and Genstone Construction received a Best of Houzz 2025 Service award.

Our executive team brings more than 60 years of combined construction industry experience, with deep expertise in REO, fix-and-flip and single-family remodeling. Behind the field work, the organization is divided into specialized teams. Estimators scope and price properties. Field managers oversee each project from start to finish. Repair specialists handle technical issues and quality. Billing produces consistent invoices and documentation. That structure lets volume move through the process without bottlenecking on any single person.

The result for institutional clients is a renovation partner whose process is the same on the first property and the five hundredth, in the first market and the twentieth, which is what makes portfolio-scale work manageable for an asset management team.

Institutional portfolios rarely sit in one city. A servicer's REO inventory follows foreclosure activity wherever it occurs. A single-family rental fund may own homes across several metros in different states. A bank's portfolio may follow its lending footprint. Managing a separate local contractor in every market means separate onboarding, separate insurance tracking, separate bid formats and separate quality standards, multiplied by every market in the portfolio.

Genstone operates on a principle of national scale and local execution. We coordinate vetted, licensed and insured local contractors from a network of thousands across a footprint of 35 states, with a particularly strong presence east of the Mississippi River. Our headquarters is in Romeoville, Illinois. In each market, the work is done by local contractors who know the housing stock, the building department and the labor market, and it is managed under one process, one quality standard and one documentation format.

For the institutional client, that means one vendor relationship instead of dozens. One onboarding. One contract structure. One set of compliance records to monitor. One reporting format across every market. One escalation path when something needs attention.

Every project still has a designated field manager responsible for it from start to finish, so accountability does not get diluted by scale. The field manager is the point of contact for the specific property, while account-level communication covers the portfolio as a whole. When a property is in a market where we have not yet worked extensively, we vet and onboard local contractors to the same standards before work begins rather than lowering the bar to fill a gap.

For an institutional owner, a contractor's compliance failure becomes the owner's problem. An uninsured subcontractor injured on site, an unpaid supplier who files a lien, unpermitted work discovered at disposition, or improper handling of lead-based paint in an older home can each create liability and reputational risk far larger than the cost of the repair.

Risk management is built into every Genstone project rather than added for institutional clients. The core elements include:

- Contractor verification. We verify that the contractors assigned to each project maintain appropriate insurance and meet applicable licensing requirements.
- Permits and inspections. Our team coordinates required permits and inspections with the local building department as part of project management, and the records are kept in the project file.
- Lien waivers. Lien waivers are collected as work is completed and paid, protecting the client's title.
- Lead-safe and environmental awareness. In homes built before 1978, work that disturbs painted surfaces follows lead-safe work practices, and suspected asbestos-containing materials in older homes are identified before they are disturbed.
- Documented change control. Changes from the approved scope are documented and approved before work proceeds.

Institutional clients usually have their own vendor management requirements, such as onboarding documentation, insurance certificates naming the client, background checks, specific coverage limits or periodic compliance reviews. We work within those requirements and supply the documentation they call for.

Because all work is coordinated under Genstone, the client sees one compliance record rather than having to monitor a scattered network of local vendors, each with its own paperwork and expiration dates.

sections.h2: Scoping, bids and approvals at scale
sections.body:
An asset manager responsible for a large portfolio cannot visit properties, so every decision rests on the bid. The bid must show the condition, describe the proposed work clearly, price it in reviewable line items and make the approval decision as easy as possible. A bid that requires follow-up calls to understand slows every approval in the queue behind it.

Our estimators produce detailed scopes with anticipated labor and materials, specific about quantities, locations and products, supported by photos of existing conditions. Dumpster and debris removal costs are included in the estimate. Where a meaningful choice exists, such as repairing or replacing a roof or heating system, the bid explains both options and their costs.

For institutional clients, bids can be adapted to the client's framework:

- Client bid templates and line-item structures.
- Client pricing schedules or agreed unit pricing where they exist.
- Repair categories such as health and safety, code compliance, financing eligibility and marketability.
- Approval thresholds that let routine work proceed and route exceptions for review.
- Client property identifiers and portfolio groupings.

Where it helps disposition decisions, we can price more than one plan for the same property, from a minimal compliance scope to a fuller renovation, so the asset manager can compare each against the expected sale price or rent.

After approval, the scope becomes the contract for the work. When unforeseen conditions appear, such as hidden water damage, failed plumbing or structural issues found during demolition, the field manager documents them with photos and a description, and a change request goes to the client before additional work proceeds.

At institutional scale, documentation is a deliverable. Asset managers report to investors, credit committees, auditors and, for GSE work, to the enterprise itself. They need to show that each repair was necessary, approved, completed as specified and paid correctly, and they need to find that record quickly months or years later.

Every Genstone project produces a consistent project file:

- The approved scope and estimate, with the draw schedule.
- Before photos supporting the bid.
- Progress photos and milestone updates, visible without a site visit.
- After photos showing each completed repair.
- Change requests with the condition found, proposed work, cost impact and approval.
- Permit and inspection records.
- Lien waivers.
- Contractor insurance and licensing verification.
- Invoices that match the approved scope and changes line by line.

Because every project follows the same structure, the files are comparable across properties and markets. That makes it possible to analyze renovation costs by market, property type and scope category, identify outliers, and build better underwriting assumptions for future acquisitions.

We adapt reporting to how the client's team works. That can mean organizing projects by fund, servicing pool, market or acquisition batch, using the client's property identifiers, meeting specific photo standards, or delivering status reporting on a regular cadence. Our billing team produces invoices and supporting documentation in a consistent format so accounts payable can process them without reconciling different vendors' formats.

Construction draws are tied to completed work, and final billing follows completion and the client's approval. No upfront payment is required.

Institutional clients engage Genstone at different stages of an asset's life, and the same relationship can cover several of them.

- REO and bank-owned repairs. Vacant property conditions, code violations, repairs to support marketing and financed buyers, and full renovations where the disposition plan justifies them. Our team has deep REO experience, and our bids are structured for remote asset manager approval.
- Acquisition renovations for rental portfolios. Bringing newly acquired single-family homes and small multifamily buildings to the owner's rent-ready standard, with consistent specifications across the portfolio.
- Capital projects on stabilized assets. Roof, heating and cooling, exterior, plumbing, electrical and drainage work, coordinated around occupied homes where needed.
- Turns and make-ready between residents. Move-out documentation, standard turn scopes and upgrades at turnover.
- Code compliance. Correcting violations and documenting their resolution with the local jurisdiction.
- FHA 203(k) work. As an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor, Genstone can support owner-occupant buyers whose purchase of a disposition property includes renovation financing.

Genstone Field Services complements the construction work with property preservation, property inspections, occupied maintenance and repairs, turn and make-ready services, and code compliance and property care. For institutional clients, that combination means one company group can protect a vacant asset, inspect it, renovate it, maintain it while occupied and turn it between residents, all with consistent documentation.

We also work with clients' existing vendors where that is the right arrangement, such as taking on renovation scopes while a separate preservation vendor remains in place. The goal is the structure that works best for the client's portfolio, not a requirement to consolidate everything.

sections.h2: The Genstone Companies and starting a relationship
sections.body:
Genstone Construction is part of the Genstone Companies, a group of businesses that together support real estate assets from acquisition through ownership and disposition. For institutional clients, several are directly relevant.

Genstone Insurance provides real estate investment insurance, including vacant property coverage, multi-property and portfolio coverage, and REIT and professional investor solutions. Title Clearing & Escrow offers title insurance, title clearance and curative services, settlement and closing services, lien release processing and post-closing loan reviews, which can be particularly relevant to servicers and lenders. Genstone Property Management provides leasing, resident screening, rent collection, maintenance coordination and owner reporting for rental portfolios. Genstone Realty supports investor brokerage, REO opportunities, and property acquisition and disposition. Genstone Financial offers DSCR rental loans, lines of credit and new construction loans. Each can be engaged independently of the others.

Institutional relationships typically begin with a conversation about the portfolio, the markets involved, the types of work needed and the client's vendor management, bidding, approval and reporting requirements. From there, many clients start with a defined set of properties or a single market, evaluate the work and the documentation, and expand as the relationship proves itself. That measured start lets both sides align on templates, thresholds and reporting before volume increases.

Completed work carries a one-year workmanship warranty. Damage caused by residents and normal wear and tear are not covered.

To discuss renovation support for a servicing portfolio, a rental fund, an REO inventory or GSE work, call Genstone Construction at (312) 429-2637 or reach out through our contact page.

faqs.q: What types of institutional clients does Genstone work with?
faqs.a: Our clients include mortgage servicers, Real Estate Investment Trusts, investment funds, banks managing REO properties and other mortgage lenders. Genstone is also a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises. We work with individual investors as well, and the same core process applies to every client, with documentation, bidding and reporting adapted to institutional requirements. Our executive team brings more than 60 years of combined construction experience, much of it in REO work.

Genstone has a footprint across 35 states, with a particularly strong presence east of the Mississippi River. Our headquarters is in Romeoville, Illinois. In each market, we coordinate vetted, licensed and insured local contractors from a network of thousands, managed under one process and standard. When a property falls in a market where we have not worked extensively, we vet and onboard local contractors to the same standard before work begins.

faqs.q: Can you meet our vendor management and insurance requirements?
faqs.a: Yes. Institutional clients often have specific onboarding documentation, insurance certificate, coverage, background check and periodic review requirements. We work within those requirements and supply the documentation they call for. Separately, we verify that the contractors assigned to each project maintain appropriate insurance and meet applicable licensing requirements, and lien waivers are collected as work is completed and paid, so the title on every asset stays clean.

faqs.q: Can you use our bid templates and pricing schedules?
faqs.a: Yes. Bids can follow your templates, line-item structures, pricing schedules or agreed unit pricing, repair categories and approval thresholds, and can use your property identifiers. Each bid includes photos of existing conditions and clear descriptions of proposed work, with options explained where a meaningful choice exists. That structure is designed to let asset managers approve routine work quickly and focus their review time on the exceptions that need it.

faqs.q: What does a completed project file include?
faqs.a: A consistent set of records for every property: the approved scope, estimate and draw schedule, before, progress and after photos, change requests with approvals, permit and inspection records, lien waivers, contractor insurance and licensing verification, and invoices that match the approved scope line by line. Files are organized by your identifiers and portfolio groupings so they can go straight into internal review or audit.

faqs.q: How are change orders handled at scale?
faqs.a: When unforeseen conditions appear, the field manager documents them with photos and a written description, and a change request with the proposed work and cost impact goes to the client for approval. No additional work proceeds until it is approved. Detailed front-end scoping by our estimators, including a close look at the conditions common in vacant and older homes, is designed to keep change requests uncommon.

faqs.q: How do institutional relationships usually start?
faqs.a: Most begin with a conversation about the portfolio, markets, types of work and the client's requirements for vendor management, bidding, approvals and reporting. Many clients then start with a defined set of properties or a single market, evaluate the work and documentation, and expand from there. That approach lets both sides align on templates and thresholds before volume increases. Call (312) 429-2637 to start the conversation.
